summary: Owners can edit an active group's name and colour from its heading or either group-menu alias. The shared dialog retains the board-local ID and both revision baselines. The preview-only PUT calls store::edit_group under selected Owner authorization; an explicit Save changes the two fields and advances both revisions in one transaction, including when the fields are unchanged.
evidence: All 37 browser_preview journeys passed serially in owned headless Chromium. browser_edits_existing_group_by_id targeted the second Work heading, preserved its non-palette colour and checked initial focus and caret at all entrances. Single-click, blank input, blur, Escape and Cancel sent no command. A board lock held the unchanged Save pending with dismissal disabled and the old grid visible. Exactly one PUT at 7/1 committed 8/2. Name-only and colour-only saves kept the other field and the same ordered children after reload.

browser_reviews_conflicting_group_edit: a deferred refusal returned 500 with the complete pre-attempt database snapshot intact before removing the fault. Peer committed 9/3; the retained 8/2 draft received 409. Review read Peer / #abcdef and both revisions for g-z; adoption sent nothing. Separate Save committed Reserve / #00c875 at 10/4. After the refresh returned 503, Reload board read the accepted state without writing. Name-only Enter and colour-only Save reached Ink / #579bfc at 12/6. Reviewing a subsequently archived target offered no adoption or replacement write.

browser_demoted_owner_cannot_edit_group: demotion after opening the dialog produced one 403 and an authorized reread. Member and Viewer could use neither alias nor heading edit, while only Member retained item editing. Membership withdrawal denied the destination and session revocation returned to sign-in. Browser checkpoints compared request paths, payloads and statuses, rendered groups and children, and fresh database snapshots including invisible roots, receipts, grants and session.

All 29 loopback_board_access cases passed. New cases covered role and grant checks, lifecycle states, route isolation, main and imported keys, UTF-16 and colour boundaries, same-ID records on different boards, and independent stale or zero baselines. Two concurrent requests yielded one 200 and one 409; replay at the old baselines conflicted. Deferred commit failure rolled back both fields and revisions. Fresh grouped and flat reads preserved [59,61,63] and full-row comparisons preserved archived and foreign children.

All 44 locked workspace tests passed, as did workspace formatting and git diff --check. Builds used target-browser-packets and the disposable database. Worker shell policy denied node --test scripts/run.test.mjs before execution. Lost PUT acknowledgments and late completions after leaving a board were not separately fault-injected.
